newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia issues toughest log export rules yet.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia issues toughest log export rules yet.

text.p: Cambodia has issued its strictest rules yet on log exports in an effort to curb continuing problems with illegal movements of timber across its borders, officials said on Thursday.

The declaration, signed by co-Premiers Hun Sen and Norodom Ranariddh and dated April 29, details the types of logs and wood products that cannot be exported and limits wood export points to Phnom Penh port and the southern coastal port of Sihanoukville.

It comes just weeks before major bilateral and multi-lateral aid agencies -- who have expressed disatisfaction with Cambodia's forestry policies -- decide how much assistance they will give Cambodia in the next year.

Last year, the International Monetary Fund cancelled a $20 million loan installment, citing a perceived lack of transparency in the government's accounting for timber revenues and a weak forestry policy.
The IMF also made $40 million in future loans contingent on improvements in Cambodia's poor forestry record.
Undersecretary of State for Agriculture May Sam Oeun acknowledged the pressure of donors and said he hoped the tough rules would crack down on deforestation.
"It will help our effort...but we have to find a way to enforce this -- it's extremely difficult," he told Reuters.
"We hope this will satisfy the IMF," he added.
Cambodia lost 1.4 million hectares (3.5 million acres) of trees between 1973 and 1993, with logging expanding each year.
In March, the IMF said it would disburse $40 million in additional loans if the government took concrete action to improve its forestry policy by May.

Also this month, major donors to Cambodia will hold a preparatory Consultative Group meeting to discuss Cambodia's progress on government reforms and logging ahead of a June meeting in Paris, when they will make aid commitments.
Separately, a local newspaper on Thursday reported that 10 employees of the Cambodian-Russian logging firm Colexim were kidnapped on Monday in the northern province of Kompong Thom.
Reaksmey Kampuchea said 10 armed bandits were demanding $30,000 for the release of the men, who were abducted while driving logging trucks.
